html:
Rabaul, a port town inside a flooded volcanic caldera on New Britain, was hit by eruptions in 1937 and again in 1994. The 1937 eruption killed about 500 people.

The town had been the capital of German New Guinea and of the Australian mandate, and the main Japanese base in the South Pacific during the Pacific War.

In September 1994 the volcanoes Tavurvur and Vulcan erupted together. Most people got out in time thanks to warnings, but ash flattened much of the town. The provincial capital was moved to Kokopo, and Rabaul never fully recovered. Tavurvur has stayed active since. Compare Tambora.
